slots.label: When it happened
slots.question: When did it happen?
slots.summary: Add a day, date, or timeframe so the moment is anchored in time.
examples: Yesterday at 3 p.m.…
On Monday around noon…

slots.label: Where and with whom
slots.question: Where did it happen and who was involved?
slots.summary: Name the space or people so the scene is easy to picture.
examples: In the conference room with Alex…
With my kids in the kitchen…

slots.label: What you directly sensed
slots.question: What did you see or hear?
slots.summary: Describe a visible action or the exact words you heard.
examples: I saw him close the laptop.
I heard “Please wrap this up.”

slots.label: Counts and quotes
slots.question: What can be counted or quoted?
slots.summary: Mention quantities or repeat the exact words when that detail matters.
examples: They called three times.
She said “I’ll handle it tomorrow.”
At (time detail) I reached to hug (other person) and they stepped back toward the doorway.
During (context detail) nobody checked how (other person) was holding up.
While (other person) wiped their eyes, the group kept typing on (object detail).
They started a meeting in (context detail) without adding me to the invite.
The door closed while I was still in the hallway.
A group chat about (context detail) went on without my name anywhere.
We agreed to have dinner at home at 7 p.m. but at 7:20 p.m. they still weren't home and had texted at 6:55 that they were staying late at work.
After three (context detail) in a row there still was no time for a break.
We skipped (context detail) to finish (context detail).
I asked for cover so I could rest and nobody was available.
While I was finishing a sentence, (other person) started talking about a different topic.
When I said I was hurt, they replied "you're overreacting" without asking more.
I asked them to repeat what they heard and they kept reading from their notes.
The project announcement went out without my name on the contributors list.
They set my proposal aside without any discussion.
We reworked the plan without explaining why the initial work did not.
The security door was propped open all evening.
The alarm panel showed the sensor offline and nobody addressed it.
They skipped the safety check before starting (context detail).
They asked me to sign immediately without time to review.
My calendar block was overwritten with another meeting.
I had to get permission before sending a routine update.
The fluorescent lights flickered through the entire evening.
There was a steady hum from the generator all night.
Our music break was canceled to squeeze in another briefing.
They asked me to tone down my description before the meeting.
My statement was edited without checking with me.
I was not allowed to mention the actual numbers during the briefing.

eventFamilies.label: A personal evaluation directed toward you
eventFamilies.explanation: The app noticed a personal evaluation directed toward you.

eventFamilies.label: Possible dismissal or minimization
eventFamilies.explanation: The app noticed wording that may dismiss or minimize an experience you described.

eventFamilies.label: An interruption while speaking
eventFamilies.explanation: The app noticed an interruption or blocked attempt to finish speaking.

eventFamilies.label: A possible exclusion or omission
eventFamilies.explanation: The app noticed an event where you or your group may have been left out.

eventFamilies.label: A decision with constrained time or choice
eventFamilies.explanation: The app noticed language about having little or no time or choice in a decision.

eventFamilies.label: A change after a prior agreement
eventFamilies.explanation: The app noticed a prior agreement followed by a change in what happened.

guidanceRules.label: A word that summarizes someone
guidanceRules.explanation: This word may describe your experience. If you want a more concrete observation too, add the words or actions that led you to use it.

guidanceRules.label: A broad description of impact
guidanceRules.explanation: If this word summarizes the result, add the specific damage or change you mean. Keep the word if it is already the most accurate description.

guidanceRules.label: A repeated pattern
guidanceRules.explanation: If you are describing a pattern, add one recent example or a count to make it easier to understand.

guidanceRules.label: A rule or judgment
guidanceRules.explanation: If this expresses what you believe should happen, also add what actually happened in this moment.

guidanceRules.label: A possible motive
guidanceRules.explanation: You may be right about the motive. If you want a concrete observation too, add the words or actions that led you to this conclusion.
terms: just to get a rise out of me

guidanceRules.label: A broad time or frequency word
guidanceRules.explanation: If you mean a repeated pattern, add a timeframe, recent example, or count when you can.

guidanceRules.label: An amount that could be more specific
guidanceRules.explanation: If the amount matters, add a count, duration, or timeframe. An estimate is fine when an exact number is not available.

guidanceRules.label: A word about impact or interpretation
guidanceRules.explanation: This word may describe your experience. If you also want a concrete observation, add the specific words, actions, or events that led you to use it.

guidanceRules.label: A figure of speech
guidanceRules.explanation: If this phrase summarizes the moment, add the words or actions you mean by it.

guidanceRules.label: A mental-health label used as a judgment
guidanceRules.explanation: If this is a diagnosis or identity, keep it as written. If it is a judgment about someone, also add the words or actions you observed.

guidanceRules.label: An uncertain conclusion
guidanceRules.explanation: Uncertainty is useful to name. You can also add the details that led you to this possibility.

guidanceRules.label: A prediction
guidanceRules.explanation: If this is about what may happen next, also add what has happened so far.

guidanceRules.label: A thought or interpretation
guidanceRules.explanation: Your thought can stay. If you want a concrete observation too, add what you saw, heard, or were told.

guidanceRules.label: A statement about blame or fault
guidanceRules.explanation: This may matter to your experience. You can also add the sequence of events that led you to describe responsibility this way.

guidanceRules.label: A statement about what was missing
guidanceRules.explanation: If you can, add the action, response, or information you expected and did not observe.

guidanceRules.label: An “I feel that…” statement
guidanceRules.explanation: This phrase usually introduces a thought. If it helps, name the emotion separately and add the event that led to the thought.

guidanceRules.label: An evaluation
guidanceRules.explanation: This evaluation can stay. You may also want to add the words, actions, or result that led you to it.

guidanceRules.label: A statement about cause or pressure
guidanceRules.explanation: If this describes pressure or coercion, add the exact words, actions, or constraints involved. This does not mean the pressure was unreal.
